playback.title: Playback
playback.intro: How Cinemion converts videos for devices that can't play the original file.
playback.savedDescription: They apply to videos started from now on.

methods.noneDescription: Convert on the CPU. Works everywhere, but 4K is slow.
methods.vaapiDescription: Intel and AMD graphics on Linux.
methods.qsvDescription: Intel graphics, often a little faster than VA-API.

playback.remoteLimitDescription: Per stream, for viewers outside your home network.
playback.toneMappingDescription: Keeps colours right on screens without HDR.
playback.seekThumbnailsDescription: Small pictures above the seek bar. Made in the background after a scan, and when a video is first played.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.intro: Where posters, plots and cast come from. Sources higher in the list win when they disagree.
metadata.savedDescription: Use "Refresh all details" on a library to apply them to what's already there.

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.intro: Search subtitles online from the player, or let Cinemion fetch them for new movies and episodes. Subtitle files next to your videos are picked up by themselves.
subtitles.autoDownloadDescription: Movies and episodes without subtitles in one of your languages get the best ones the sites have, preferring ones made for the exact file. What isn't found is looked for again after a day, three days, a week, and so on.
subtitles.noSite: Turn on at least one subtitle site below for this to find anything.
subtitles.openSubtitlesHelp: Create a free account on <link>opensubtitles.com</link>, then add an API consumer under your profile's API settings and paste its key here. Signing in is optional; it raises the number of downloads per day.
subtitles.passwordSaved: Saved. Type a new one to change it.
subtitles.subdlHelp: A free site with a big catalogue. Make an account on <link>subdl.com</link> and copy the API key from your account page.
subtitles.podnapisiDescription: Search podnapisi.net too. It needs no account; its subtitles are found by title, so their timing may be a little off.
subtitles.languagesDescription: Offered first when searching, and the ones downloaded by themselves.
subtitles.saveNextToVideo: Save next to the video file
subtitles.saveNextToVideoDescription: Off, or when the media folder is read-only (as in Docker with :ro), downloads are kept in the config folder instead.

games.title: Games
games.intro: Clips libraries sort clips into games by their file and folder names, and look the games up for their proper names, covers and artwork.
games.lookupsDescription: On Steam's store, which needs no key and knows most PC games.
games.steamGridDbDescription: Finds games that aren't on Steam, like VALORANT or League of Legends, and artwork Steam doesn't have. Get a free key from your <link>SteamGridDB preferences</link>.

recognition.title: Picture recognition
recognition.intro: For clips whose names don't say the game, like OBS recordings: Cinemion looks at a few frames of every clip and suggests a game when a clip looks like ones you've already given a game (or, as a best guess, like a game it knows). Suggestions are only taken when you say so. It runs on this server's processor, a clip at a time, and nothing leaves the server.

recognition.removeDescription: The download is deleted. Suggestions already made stay, and what it saw in clips is kept for when it's downloaded again.
recognition.startedDescription: Suggestions show up on clips without a game. Tasks shows how far it is.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.intro: Work Cinemion does in the background, and when it scans your libraries by itself.

scan.title: Scan all libraries
scan.text: Look for new, changed and removed files in every library.

refresh.title: Refresh all details
refresh.text: Fetch details and artwork again for every title. This takes a while on big libraries.

thumbnails.title: Make missing seek thumbnails
thumbnails.text: The pictures that show while you drag through a video. New videos get them by themselves.

markers.title: Find intros and credits again
markers.text: Compare every season's episodes and read chapters again, for Skip intro and starting the next episode early. New episodes are looked at by themselves.

subtitles.title: Download missing subtitles
subtitles.text: Look for subtitles in your languages for every movie and episode that has none, even ones searched lately. With automatic downloads on, this also happens once a day.

remake.title: Remake all seek thumbnails
remake.text: Delete every seek thumbnail and make them again, one video at a time.
remake.confirmDescription: Every video gets new thumbnails, one after another. Until a video's turn comes, it has none.

tasks.scanEveryDescription: New files usually show up within a minute anyway. Scheduled scans catch what the folder watcher misses, like changes on network shares.
tasks.nothingFinished: Nothing has finished since the server started.

intro.one: The last {count} line of the server log, newest first. Handy when something doesn't work.
intro.other: The last {count} lines of the server log, newest first. Handy when something doesn't work.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.intro: Let Sonarr and Radarr tell Cinemion about new downloads, so they show up right away, connect apps like Seerr and Homepage, and let profiles keep their Trakt history up to date.
integrations.copyItByHand: Select it and copy it by hand.

arr.title: Sonarr and Radarr
arr.copyByHand: Select the address and copy it by hand.
arr.localhostHint: You opened Cinemion as {host}, which Sonarr and Radarr can't reach from another computer or container. Open Cinemion through its network address (like {example}) and copy the address from there.

steps.connect: In Sonarr or Radarr, open Settings → Connect, click + and pick Webhook.
steps.paste: Paste the address above into URL and leave the method on POST.
steps.events: Tick On File Import, On File Upgrade, On Rename and the Delete events.
steps.test: Click Test. Cinemion shows below that it arrived.

newAddress.title: New address
newAddress.text: If the address got out, make a new one. The old one stops working, so paste the new one into Sonarr and Radarr.
newAddress.madeDescription: Paste it into Sonarr and Radarr again.
newAddress.confirmDescription: Sonarr and Radarr can't reach Cinemion with the old address anymore until you paste the new one into them.

mappings.title: Path mappings
mappings.text: Only needed when Sonarr or Radarr see your media in a different folder than Cinemion does, like {theirs} in their container and {ours} here. Folders inside a mapped folder are mapped too.

apps.title: Seerr, Homepage and other apps
apps.text: Apps made for other media servers can use Cinemion instead. In Seerr, pick the media server that signs in with a server address, username and password, give it the address below, and sign in with your Cinemion login: it sees what's in your libraries and links back here. Homepage's media server widget can show what's playing and how big your libraries are with a key made below.
apps.madeByRemoved: Made {ago} by a profile that has been removed, so it doesn't work
apps.removedDescription: {app} can't reach Cinemion with it anymore.
apps.confirmDescription: The app using it can't reach Cinemion anymore until it gets a new key.

podium.title: Podium
podium.text: Podium can upload clips straight into a library. Make a target for each library to upload to, then add a Podium-compatible server in Podium with the server URL and the target's token. Clips keep the game Podium recorded, their title, when they were recorded and the names of their sound tracks. Podium uploads into any library; Clips libraries make the most of what it knows.
podium.libraryRemoved: Its library was removed, so it doesn't work
podium.creatorRemoved: Made by a profile that has been removed, so it doesn't work
podium.intoGames: Into {where}, a folder per game · last used {ago}
podium.intoGamesNotUsed: Into {where}, a folder per game · not used yet
podium.uploadsInto: Uploads go into this folder inside {path}. Cinemion needs write access to it, like for uploads from the browser.
podium.uploadsIntoFirst: Uploads go into this folder inside the library's first folder. Cinemion needs write access to it, like for uploads from the browser.
podium.gameFoldersDescription: Puts each clip in a folder named after its game, the way recorders do.
podium.removedDescription: Podium can't upload with its token anymore.
podium.confirmDescription: Podium can't upload with its token anymore. What it uploaded stays in the library.

trakt.title: Trakt
trakt.text: With a Trakt app, every profile can link its own Trakt account: what they watch is scrobbled, and what they mark watched shows up in their Trakt history. Make the app at {link} with {redirect} as its redirect URI, then copy its keys here.
trakt.setUpDescription: Profiles can link their accounts in Settings › Your profile.

email.title: Email
email.text: Lets Cinemion email profiles that want their notifications by email. Use your mail provider's SMTP server, or one on your network.
email.testFailed: The test email didn't go out

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: Send events like "playback started" to other apps, such as Home Assistant or a chat bot.

empty.title: No webhooks yet
empty.text: A webhook is an address Cinemion sends a short JSON message to whenever something you pick happens. Dim the lights when a movie starts, or post new episodes to a chat.

developers.title: For developers
developers.text: Each event is a {method} with a JSON body: {body}. The {header} header is {prefix} followed by the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the webhook's secret, so the receiver can check it came from this server. Failed sends are tried again after 10 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes.

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.description: Cinemion stops sending events to this address.

dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameDescription: Optional. Defaults to the address's host.
dialog.secretLater: A secret for checking signatures is made when you add the webhook.
dialog.addedDescription: Use Send test to check that it arrives.
dialog.newSecretDescription: Update it in the receiving app too.
dialog.copyByHand: Select it and copy it by hand.

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.intro: The folders Cinemion looks in for movies, shows, other videos, music and books. New files are picked up by themselves.
libraries.conflict: {conflict} Use “Edit library” to change the folders.

adding.one: Adding an upload to the library

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.description: Cinemion forgets this library and its watch history. The files in its folders are not touched.

videos.name: Videos
videos.description: For home videos, recordings and anything else that isn't a movie or show. Nothing is looked up online: titles come from the file names, and you can edit the details by hand.

music.name: Music
music.description: Albums, artists and tracks, sorted by the tags in the files (or folders like Artist/Album/01 Title.mp3). Covers come from the files or a cover.jpg next to them, and lyrics from tags or .lrc files. Nothing is looked up online.

photos.name: Photos
photos.description: Photos and phone videos, with every folder as an album. Dates, cameras and places come from the photos themselves (HEIC from iPhones works too), and nothing is looked up online. Everyone can also make their own albums without moving any files.

clips.name: Clips
clips.description: Game recordings, grouped by game. The game comes from the names recorders give their files and folders (NVIDIA, AMD, Xbox Game Bar, OBS, Steam and more), with covers from Steam. Clips without a game can be given one by hand, or get a suggestion from picture recognition.

audiobooks.name: Audiobooks
audiobooks.description: A folder of audio files is one book (parts in CD1, CD2… folders too), and so is a single .m4b. Chapters come from the files, details from their tags, and everyone keeps their own place.

books.name: Books
books.description: EPUB books are read right in Cinemion, with everyone's place saved; PDFs open in the browser's own viewer. Details and covers come from the files.

videos.label: Rating for unrated videos
videos.description: Profiles with an age limit only see videos rated within it. Pick “{rating}” for family videos everyone may see.

music.label: Rating for these albums
music.description: Profiles with an age limit only see music rated within it. Pick “{rating}” so everyone can listen.

photos.label: Rating for unrated photos
photos.description: Profiles with an age limit only see photos and videos rated within it. Pick “{rating}” for family photos everyone may see.

clips.label: Rating for unrated clips
clips.description: Profiles with an age limit only see clips rated within it. Pick one that suits the games you play, like “{rating}”.

books.label: Rating for these books
books.description: Profiles with an age limit only see books rated within it. Pick “{rating}” so everyone can read and listen.

rating.none: None: hide them from age-limited profiles

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.rescanNote: After saving, the libraries are scanned again. Titles in folders you removed leave this library, along with their watch history here.

dialog.title: Upload to {name}
dialog.description: Files go into the folder you pick. Zip files are unpacked there, keeping the folders inside them. Uploads keep going when you close this.
dialog.newFolderDescription: Use / for a folder inside a folder. It's made when the upload starts.
dialog.openFolder: Open the folder to upload into.
dialog.drop: Drop files, folders or zip files here
dialog.replace: Replace files that are already there
dialog.replaceDescription: Otherwise a file that's already in the folder isn't uploaded, and zip files leave those files out.
dialog.cantCarryOn: Can't carry on with that file

accepts.video: Video files, subtitles, NFO files and pictures, or zip files with them.
accepts.music: Audio files, lyrics and covers, or zip files with them.
accepts.audiobooks: Audio files, cue sheets, descriptions and covers, or zip files with them.
accepts.books: EPUB and PDF files and covers, or zip files with them.
accepts.photos: Photos (JPG, HEIC, PNG and more) and videos, or zip files with them.
accepts.clips: Video files, subtitles and pictures, or zip files with them.

skip.notUsed: Not a file this library uses

folderErrors.outside: The new folder has to be inside the folder above.
folderErrors.hidden: Folder names starting with a dot are hidden, so the library would never show them.

status.paused: Stopped at {percent}%. Pick the file again to carry on.

errors.tooLarge: The piece was too large for the server or a proxy in front of it.
errors.connectionLost: Lost the connection to the server.

differentFile.one: That's a different file. Pick "{name}" ({count} byte) to carry on.
differentFile.other: That's a different file. Pick "{name}" ({count} bytes) to carry on.

errors.differentContents: That file has different contents from the one being uploaded.

updates.title: Updates
updates.versions: This server has {current}. The new one came out {date}.

how.docker: To update, get the new image and start the container again, for example with {command}. Your libraries and settings stay as they are.
how.aur: To update, upgrade the {package} package (for example with {upgrade}), then restart Cinemion with {restart}.
how.binary: To update, download the new version from the release page, put it in place of this one and start Cinemion again. Your libraries and settings stay as they are.
how.source: To update, get the new version with {command} and start Cinemion again.

updates.checksSoon: Cinemion checks a minute after it starts.
updates.switchDescription: Looks at Cinemion's releases on GitHub twice a day and tells admins when there's a new one. Nothing about your server or libraries is sent, and nothing is installed by itself.
updates.disabledByEnv: Turned off for this server with {setting}.

credits.tmdb: This product uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Keep a copy of everything Cinemion can't get back by itself: profiles, what everyone watched, settings, playlists, albums and the details you edited.
backups.none: No backups yet. Make one now, or turn on a schedule below.
backups.confirmDeleteDescription: The backup from {date} will be gone for good.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.label: Make a backup by itself
schedule.keepDescription: Older scheduled backups are deleted. Ones you make by hand are kept until you delete them.
schedule.next: The next one is due {when}, at night when possible.
schedule.lastFailed: The last scheduled backup didn't work: {error}
schedule.beforeUpdates: Cinemion also makes a backup by itself before an update changes its database, so you can go back. It keeps the last three of those.

contents.title: What goes in
contents.text: Every backup has the database, the sign-in key, profile pictures and artwork you picked or uploaded by hand. Conversions, seek thumbnails and other things in the cache are left out; they're made again when needed.
contents.artworkDescription: Posters and backdrops from the internet. Backups get bigger, but a restored server looks complete straight away instead of after a refresh of all details.
contents.folderDescription: A full path on the server. Leave it empty to use the folder shown. A folder on another drive keeps your backups safe if this one fails.
contents.folderSaved: Backups will go in the new folder

password.on: Backups are protected with a password
password.text: A backup holds the sign-in key and the keys of the services you connected, so anyone with the file could get into this server. A password locks new backups; without it they can't be restored, so keep it somewhere safe.
password.removeDescription: New backups won't need a password. Backups that were protected still need the old one.
password.saved: New backups will be protected with this password
password.dialogDescription: New backups will need this password to be restored. Backups made before keep the password they had.

restore.title: Restoring a backup
restore.text: A restore replaces everything on a server with what's in the backup, so it's done while nothing else is going on:
restore.wizard: On a new or reinstalled Cinemion, pick “Restore a backup” on the first page of the setup. It finds backups in the backup folder, or you can upload one.
restore.cli: On this server, stop Cinemion and run {command}, then start it again.

myList.title: My list
myList.intro: Movies and shows you want to watch. Add them with the bookmark button on their page.
myList.waitingText: These are on your list but not in any library you can see. They move up by themselves once they're added.

empty.title: Nothing on your list yet
empty.text: Found something for later? Press the bookmark button on its page and it shows up here and on the home screen.

trakt.synced: Your list is in step with Trakt
trakt.syncedAgo: Kept in step with your Trakt watchlist, both ways. Last synced {ago}.
trakt.notYet: Kept in step with your Trakt watchlist, both ways. The first sync happens in a few minutes.
trakt.failed: The last sync with Trakt didn't work: {error}
trakt.notLinked: Link Trakt in <link>Settings › Your profile</link> to keep this list in step with your Trakt watchlist.

https.title: HTTPS
https.intro: A secure address for Cinemion, without setting up a reverse proxy. Browsers need it for offline downloads and for notifications on phones.

address.title: Secure address
address.switchDescription: Cinemion also answers on a second port, encrypted. The plain http address keeps working next to it.
address.portDescription: 8443 unless something else uses it. With Docker, publish this port too.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.facts: From {issuer}, valid until {date}. It's renewed by itself before it runs out.

cinemion.text: Works on any home network, no domain needed. Cinemion signs its own certificate, so each device has to trust Cinemion once (see below); until then browsers warn about the address.
cinemion.namesDescription: Cinemion covers this computer's name and addresses by itself. Add others it's reached at, like a name your router hands out or the computer's address when Cinemion runs in Docker.
cinemion.notCovered: You opened this page at {host}, which the certificate doesn't cover yet.
cinemion.added: The certificate now covers that address

trust.title: Trust Cinemion on your devices
trust.text: Do this once on every device that opens Cinemion over https. It makes the device trust certificates this Cinemion signs, and nothing else.
trust.onPhone: On a phone or tablet, open {address} in its browser to download it there.

windows.title: Windows
windows.steps:
Open the downloaded file and choose Install Certificate.
Pick Local Machine, then Place all certificates in the following store, Browse, and Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
Finish, then restart the browser.

mac.title: Mac
mac.steps:
Open the downloaded file; Keychain Access adds it to the login keychain.
Double-click the certificate there, open Trust, and set When using this certificate to Always Trust.
Close the window and enter your password to save.

iphone.title: iPhone and iPad
iphone.steps:
Open the download address in Safari and allow the profile to download.
Go to Settings › General › VPN & Device Management, open the Cinemion profile and install it.
Then go to Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings and switch on full trust for Cinemion.

android.title: Android
android.steps:
Download the file in the browser.
Go to Settings › Security › More security settings (or Encryption & credentials) › Install a certificate › CA certificate, and pick the file.
The wording differs a little between phones; searching Settings for "certificate" finds it.

linux.title: Linux
linux.steps:
Arch: sudo trust anchor cinemion-ca.crt
Debian and Ubuntu: copy the file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run sudo update-ca-certificates.
Chrome on Linux keeps its own list: Settings › Privacy and security › Security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import.

firefox.title: Firefox (any computer)
firefox.steps: Firefox has its own list. Go to Settings › Privacy & Security › Certificates › View Certificates › Authorities › Import, pick the file and tick Trust this CA to identify websites.

letsencrypt.text: A certificate every device trusts straight away, free from Let's Encrypt, for a domain of your own that points at this server.
letsencrypt.stepDomain: Point the domain (or a subdomain) at your home's internet address.
letsencrypt.stepPort80: Forward port 80 on your router to port {port} on this computer. Let's Encrypt checks the domain through it, again every couple of months.
letsencrypt.stepPort443: Forward port 443 to the https port {port}, so the domain opens Cinemion over https.
letsencrypt.emailDescription: Let's Encrypt writes here if a certificate is about to run out without being renewed.
letsencrypt.terms: Getting a certificate means agreeing to <link>Let's Encrypt's subscriber agreement</link>.
letsencrypt.done: Let's Encrypt handed out a certificate

own.text: Already have a certificate, from your router, your own certificate authority or a wildcard for your domain? Paste it here. You'll have to replace it yourself before it runs out.
own.certificateDescription: PEM text, with the intermediate certificates after your own (the full chain).

redirect.title: Plain http
redirect.description: Pages opened at the http address move to the https one. Apps, Sonarr, Radarr and webhooks keep using http as before. Only turn this on once your devices trust the certificate.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty: Nothing new yet. New movies, episodes and titles from your list show up here.
notifications.fromList: From your list, now here to watch

prefs.title: Notifications
prefs.modeDescription: New movies, episodes, albums and books in the libraries you can see. Titles from My list always count.
prefs.following: Shows I watch and titles on My list
prefs.pushDescription: Get them like messages from other apps, also when Cinemion isn't open.
prefs.pushUnavailable: This server can't send push notifications right now.
prefs.pushNeedsHttps: This browser can only get them when Cinemion is opened over https (Settings › HTTPS). iPhones and iPads need Cinemion added to the home screen first.
prefs.pushDenied: The browser was told not to show notifications from Cinemion. Allow them in the browser's site settings, then try again.
prefs.pushNoWorker: Reload the page once and try again; the part that receives notifications wasn't running yet.
prefs.testNone: No device took the test. Turn notifications off and on again on the device.
prefs.emailDescription: Leave empty for no email. You get one email per batch of new things.

stats.title: Your stats
stats.intro: What you watched, listened to and read, and how long for.
stats.everyoneIntro: The whole household's time, the favourites, and what nobody watches.
stats.emptyText: Watch, listen or read something and the time shows up here.
stats.chartLabel: Time per day or month, split into watching, listening and reading

privateProfiles.one: 1 profile keeps its stats private; its time counts in the totals.
privateProfiles.other: {count} profiles keep their stats private; their time counts in the totals.

untouched.title: What nobody watches
untouched.text: Movies and shows that nobody on this server ever played.

private.label: Keep my stats private
private.description: Leaves your name out of everyone's stats and the household's year in review. Your time still counts in the totals, without your name.

review.title: {year} in review
review.emptyText: Nothing was watched, heard or read in {year} yet.
